newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 2.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- The economy is heading into its seventh year of expansion, but it will be growing at a slower rate than in the previous 12 months.
- The Dow Jones industrials ended 1996 with a 26 percent gain.
- Doubletree agreed to acquire Renaissance Hotel Group for about $780 million in cash and stock, plus the assumption of $70 million in debt.
- Consumer confidence rose to its highest level in seven years in December.
- Horizon/CMS said it paid the federal government $5.8 million to resolve an investigation into allegations of Medicare and Medicaid fraud at the chain of nursing homes.
- Express freight carriers said volume during the peak holiday shipping season grew moderately from a year earlier.
- Northeast Utilities' management was blasted for its poor nuclear safety program in a review ordered by Connecticut regulators.
- Some analysts are more bullish on Canadian stocks than American for 1997.
- Finland's stock market jumped 47 percent in 1996.
- Morton International said it agreed to pay $290 million to acquire French salt maker Salins du Midi.
- Privatizations reached a record $43 billion in Western Europe last year.
- General Motors is challenging a request from the IRS that it pay an additional $335 million in taxes for 1985.
- News of strength in housing and manufacturing dealt a flurry of telling punches to Treasury prices during an abbreviated day in the bond market Tuesday.
